opportunities.title: [FEATURE] asm audit security: flag MCP server and hook configs shipped inside a skill
opportunities.excerpt:
<!-- idd:normalized v1 -->

## Type

feature

## Description

`asm audit security` reports a skill as safe when the skill ships an MCP server config. In the repro below, the config starts an unpinned remote package and passes it a credential from the environment. `asm install` prints no warning either, because it shows the same scan's results.

Uber's skills platform blocks `.mcp.json` inside skills and plugins. A tool server preloads every tool definition into each call (Uber measured 50,000–70,000 tokens for 100+ tools), and an unpinned `npx -y …@latest` server is a supply-chain path *(practitioner: Uber Engineering, "How Uber Evals 1 Million Agent Skill Invocations a Month", 2026-11-23)*.

Found while dogfooding (asm v2.25.0 @ 68f2e89, which already includes #882's new audit rules).

Repro (sandboxed HOME):

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/mcp-skill/scripts
printf -- '---\nname: mcp-skill\ndescription: "Query the helper server when the user asks for helper data. Not for writes."\n---\n# MCP skill\n' > /tmp/mcp-skill/SKILL.md
echo '{"mcpServers":{"helper":{"command":"npx","args":["-y","some-unpinned-mcp-server@latest"],"env":{"TOKEN":"${GITHUB_TOKEN}"}}}}' > /tmp/mcp-skill/.mcp.json
asm audit security /tmp/mcp-skill --json
```

**Current behavior:**
Verdict `safe`, "No suspicious patterns detected."

**Expected behavior:**
The audit lists every server the skill would start (its command line), and raises the verdict according to the rules below.

**Related issues:**
#782 (audit never scans SKILL.md/.md instructions; this issue is about JSON configs), #882

> **Reporter Context**
> Found by Smith during the Uber skill-evals gap analysis (idea V26).

## Screenshots

n/a

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A skill folder containing `.mcp.json` or `mcp.json`, or a plugin/agent manifest whose top level holds `mcpServers`, gets a finding in a new category that names each server and its full command line. The verdict is at least `warning`
- [ ] The verdict is `dangerous` when a server command fetches remote code without a pinned version (`npx -y`, `uvx`, `pipx run`, `@latest`, or no version) or passes an environment variable whose name looks like a credential (TOKEN, KEY, SECRET, PASSWORD)
- [ ] A `settings.json` (or another agent config) holding `hooks` gets the same treatment: listed, verdict at least `warning`

opportunities.title: [security] MCP column masking is bypassed by SQL Server FOR JSON / FOR XML and PostgreSQL query_to_xml / table_to_xml / schema_to_xml / database_to_xml: a «Lectura» assistant gets protected values in clear
opportunities.excerpt:
## What happens

The protected values are returned in clear inside one JSON/XML cell, for one table or (schema_to_xml / database_to_xml) for every table at once.

## Expected

The query is refused (or the protected values come back as [oculto]), as for `SELECT password FROM <t>` or `SELECT t FROM <t> t`.

## Steps to reproduce

1) In a data folder, connections.json with a SQL Server and a PostgreSQL connection, mcp.json enabled with level "read". 2) Create a table with a column named password holding a value. 3) Over MCP call run_query with `SELECT * FROM <t> FOR JSON AUTO` (SQL Server) or `SELECT table_to_xml('<t>', true, false, '')` (PostgreSQL).

## Evidence

Location: [`src-tauri/src/mcp.rs#L1023`](../blob/feat/integration-2.5.0/src-tauri/src/mcp.rs#L1023)

review-out/security/mcp-masking-probes.txt (celer.exe --mcp --data-dir <scratch>, level «Lectura», default redact pattern, table sec_probe(id, name, password='hunter2-SECRET')). Control `SELECT * FROM sec_probe` returns password as "[oculto]" on SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite. But on SQL Server `SELECT * FROM sec_probe FOR JSON AUTO` returns [{"id":1,"name":"alice","password":"hunter2-SECRET"}], `... FOR XML PATH` returns <password>hunter2-SECRET</password>, and `SELECT (SELECT * FROM sec_probe FOR JSON PATH) AS j` also does. On PostgreSQL `SELECT query_to_xml('SELECT * FROM sec_probe', true, false, '')`, `SELECT table_to_xml('sec_probe', true, false, '')` and `SELECT schema_to_xml('public', true, false, '')` return every protected value of the table / whole schema. Code path: check_read_access (mcp.rs:1996) only refuses queries that name a protected column (query_identifiers) or match masking_bypass (mcp.rs:1023: whole-row refs, column alias lists, UNION/INTERSECT/EXCEPT). FOR JSON/FOR XML is let through by check_read_tokens (mcp.rs:800-806 only refuses FOR UPDATE/SHARE/KEY/NO), the table name inside a string literal is invisible to the lexer, and the result column (JSON_F52E2B61-…, query_to_xml, table_to_xml, j) does not match the redact pattern, so rows_json masks nothing. The docs caveat (AI_MCP.md:44-45) only mentions views or functions that rename a column, not built-in one-liners that serialise the whole table.

## Fix hint

opportunities.title: Claude Code adapter: a trust dialog that warns of hooks in .claude/skills or .claude/agents is not recognised
opportunities.excerpt:
Found in the review of #848 (#752), reproduced with Claude Code 2.1.332. Not changed there.

A repository whose skill, command or agent declares hooks in its front matter gets a folder-trust dialog with the hooks warning, naming a directory and not a settings file, and no line naming files:

```
 Claude Code'll be able to read, edit, and execute files here.

 ⚠ This folder configures hooks that can run commands without asking, declared
 in .claude/skills

 Security guide

 ❯ No, exit
   Yes, I trust this folder
```

(`.claude/skills` with a `.claude/skills/x/SKILL.md`, `.claude/agents` with a `.claude/agents/x.md`; by the program text also `.claude/commands`, and together with the settings files.)

The adapter reads the hooks warning only when the line "Trusting this folder loads" names what it declares, so this screen gets no key and no event: the start ends at the start timeout with raw terminal output. No `trust_files` entry helps, and a person is not told that hooks are why. In a confined session the dialog has no warning and is answered.

By the program text (not reproduced), a dialog for the home folder says one more sentence, "This is your home folder, so Yes lasts for this session only.", and is not read either.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Real captures of the dialog whose warning names `.claude/skills` and `.claude/agents`, alone and with a settings file, are read: refused naming them, or answered when all are trusted, as the owner decides for what `trust_files` may name. The tests fail on main.
- [ ] Any other directory there, or any other text, gets no key.

Related: #592, #752, #758.

inboundFeedback.title: [Agent trial] Maintainer assignment: preserve SIGINT child exit status in cage relay
inboundFeedback.body:
Maintainer-assigned real engineering task for the resident. This is not external adoption feedback.

Observed on the current source: src/cage/relay.js exits with 143 when its child terminates with SIGINT. The relay's stated contract is to leave with the child's exit status; the conventional shell status for SIGINT is 128 + 2 = 130.

Reproduction (run from the repository, Node on Linux/macOS):

```js
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
const result = spawnSync(process.execPath, [
  'src/cage/relay.js', '/tmp/unused-agenthub-task.sock', '0', '--',
  process.execPath, '-e', "process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGINT')"
], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 5000 });
console.log(result.status); // observed 143; expected 130
```

The unused Unix socket is never contacted by this reproduction. Port 0 requests an ephemeral loopback port. No external service or credentials are needed.

Acceptance:
- Independently reproduce the baseline failure with a new regression test.
- Correct source behavior without editing existing tests, the controller, workflows or manifests.
- Preserve ordinary numeric child exit codes, SIGTERM=143 and SIGKILL=137.
- The exact regression must fail before the change and pass after it; the complete existing suite must pass.
- Save a candidate branch/PR with actual execution evidence. Do not claim success from a proposed patch or model review.

Start with src/cage/relay.js. Do not pursue the earlier unverified port-binding-race hypothesis for this task. If blocked, record the actual tool error and checkpoint.

This task tests one useful repair, not autonomous general intelligence or adoption.
